title: Mapping Hope Workshop (AGIT 2026)
content:
Geospatial Technology & Peacebuilding in Sub-Saharan Africa

July 7–8, 2026 | Organized by PeaceEye FlexCo

As part of the lead-up to the AGIT 2026 Conference, PeaceEye is proud to host Mapping Hope, a 2-day workshop and a collaborative space where geospatial researchers, peacebuilding practitioners, policy actors, and the PeaceTech industry come together around a shared purpose: advancing conflict prevention, digital inclusion, and locally grounded innovation across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Day One · July 7 · 10:00 – 11:00 CEST

Online Panel Discussion | Mapping for Conflict Prevention and Governance

This online panel session bridges geospatial technology, policy, and peacebuilding, exploring how spatial data and mapping tools can drive more peaceful, equitable outcomes across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Confirmed Panelists:

    • Johannes Maerk – Ideaz Institute Vienna / University of Applied Sciences Campus Vienna 
    • Yann Rebois – Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
    • Lars Wirkus – BICC
    • Evelyne Atieno Owino – BICC
    • Opeyemi Kazeem-Jimoh – PeaceEye FlexCo
  • Johannes Maerk – Ideaz Institute Vienna / University of Applied Sciences Campus Vienna 
  • Yann Rebois – Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)

title: The Data Mosaic for Peace (The Peace Room)
content:
This blog post highlights a recently published article in The Peace Room Substack, where PeaceEye CEO, Andreas Papp, discusses the vision behind PeaceEye’s Data Integration Platform, particularly its main differentiator, the Local Intelligence Component.

The data mosaic

”

PeaceEye’s architecture starts with Earth Observation data from the Copernicus program, the EU’s satellite constellation. That gives the platform the ability to detect physical changes on the ground, like burned structures, troop movements, population displacement patterns, movement in mines that are allegedly closed, infrastructure damage, and environmental shifts like access to water or changes in land use. This is layered with open-source intelligence, including near-real-time media monitoring and social media sentiment analysis, and AI-driven analytics that fuse these data streams into geospatial risk assessments.

But Papp is the first to say that’s not enough to understand what’s happening on the ground. “Without human intelligence, we would miss one of the most important pieces of information,” he says. “What is going on the ground that we don’t see on satellites.”

title: PeaceEye-FUNAAB Sign MoU on Farmer-Herder Conflict Tool
content:
In a bold move to resolve the lingering farmer-herder crisis in Nigeria, the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), today, January 19, 2026, entered into a strategic partnership with PeaceEye FlexCo, an Austria-based geospatial intelligence and digital innovation company, to develop a technology-driven Farmer–Herder App aimed at preventing and mitigating conflicts across Nigeria.

The partnership formalised with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), marked a significant step towards deploying research-led, inclusive digital solutions to one of sub-Saharan Africa’s most persistent socio-economic and security challenges.

Farmer–herder conflicts have intensified across Nigeria in recent years, driven by climate change, declining land productivity, water scarcity, and shifting migration patterns. These pressures have heightened competition over land and natural resources, resulting in recurring violence, displacement, and economic losses. The FUNAAB–PeaceEye collaboration seeks to address these challenges through innovation, data-driven planning, and community engagement.

title: From the Horse’s Mouth. Meeting with Farmers and Herders in Nigeria.
content:
Last week in Ogun State, Nigeria, PeaceEye’s CEO, Andreas Papp, met directly with herder and farmer communities in their villages to discuss how technology can help prevent conflict without violence. Across Nigeria’s Middle Belt, farmer–herder conflicts are escalating, driven by climate change, land pressure, and shrinking grazing corridors.

Listening to local leaders share their daily challenges, needs, and vulnerabilities was truly inspiring. With the support of Prof. Busari and Prof. Oyedepoja from FUNAAB University, and with the trust and consent of both communities, we agreed to continue developing solutions through co-creation, with communities at the center.

Together with our academic partners (FUNAAB University, Ladoke Akintola University of Technology & Akwa Ibom State University), my colleague Muyiwa Ezekiel Oshundele and I have explored what a practical, tech-based solution to prevent further violence could look like.

More details here.

title: A Digital Approach To Farmer-Herder Conflict in Nigeria With PeaceEye
content:
Farmer-herder conflict in Nigeria is often talked about as if it is inevitable, rooted in identity or ancient rivalries. But when you look closer, what you see is something much more practical and much more solvable: people struggling to share shrinking land, disrupted routes, and increasingly fragile livelihoods. This piece looks at what is really driving violence in Nigeria’s Middle Belt, and how small, everyday uncertainties about land, movement, and access can spiral into deadly conflict. It also shares how PeaceEye is using simple digital tools to reduce those risks on teh ground, turning conflict data into clearer routes, clearer boundaries, and fewer dangerous misunderstandings.

When people talk about farmer–herder conflict in Nigeria, it is often framed as an ethnic or cultural problem. That framing is convenient, but it is also misleading. What is unfolding across large parts of the country, particularly in the Middle Belt, is not driven by identity alone. It is driven by land, movement, survival, and a growing mismatch between how people have lived for generations and the realities they now face.

title: PeaceEye presents at AfricaGIS 2025
content:
It was a pleasure to attend the #AfricaGIS2025 Conference in Accra, Ghana, held from 17–21 November 2025. The event brought together government leaders, industry professionals, and researchers from across the African continent to explore the theme “Harnessing Geospatial Intelligence for Africa’s Sustainable and Resilient Future.”

PeaceEye's presentation: Geospatial Intelligence for Conflict Risk Resilience in Africa.

During the conference, PeaceEye FlexCo had the opportunity to present on “Geospatial Intelligence for Conflict Risk Resilience in Africa,” highlighting our commitment to advancing data–driven peacebuilding across the continent.

We shared insights from our preliminary work in South Sudan and Sudan, along with upcoming initiatives in Nigeria on topics such as herder-farmer conflict and election-related risks. These efforts are strengthened by our collaborations with local stakeholders, government agencies, and universities eager to support this mission.

Arioluwa represented PeaceEye at the conference

title: ESA Acceleration Days
content:
Grateful to have been part of ESAAccelerationDays. Happy to see how open collaboration and shared purpose can turn ideas into real impact.

Working together with Matthias Traub (Invenium Data Insights GmbH), and Georg Rinnhofer (World-Direct eBusiness solutions GmbH), supported remotely by Z_GIS – Department of Geoinformatics, University of Salzburg, once again showed of how much can happen when people from different fields unite around one goal – in our case providing emergency coordinators with near real-time insights from satellite data and mobile phone floating data to help saving lives.

Like the claim “Accelerate Crisis Preparedness” – strengthening preparedness and the hands-on management of emergencies through EO-based solutions – at PeaceEye FlexCo, this is exactly what we’re building.

Congratulations to the winners Trillium Technologies and to all the other competing teams. We all agreed at the end, the only thing we missed was to get to know each other better.

title: Everything begins with ground truth | PeaceEye visited Nigeria
content:
Last week in Nigeria, I had the opportunity to stand alongside my colleague Muyiwa Ezekiel Oshundele, representatives from LAUTECH and AKSU, the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA), and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) — where we reaffirmed our commitment to strengthening cooperation on conflict prevention and early response.

These encounters once again highlighted what bottom-up truly means: learning from those who understand the realities and needs of affected communities best, building trust, and co-creating solutions that deliver sustainable impact for people on the ground.

Through PeaceEye FlexCo, I aim to bridge these perspectives — turning geospatial and local insights into actionable information for both local stakeholders and international decision-makers. In real time. Driven by needs on the ground.

Standing among such dedicated professionals was a powerful reminder that peace starts with understanding and trust — and grows when knowledge, empathy, and technology come together.

More to come as we continue exploring how collaboration and geospatial intelligence can help prevent conflicts before they arise.

title: PeaceEye won the CASSINI Challenge – Idea Track!
content:
The 2024 CASSINI Challenge, under the theme “Make it with Space!”, was looking for solutions that use space technologies to solve real-world problems. From satellite navigation and Earth observation to secure communications and space surveillance and tracking, participants showed their innovation and commercial potential across the 3 competition tracks: Idea, Prototype and Product.

PeaceEye was one of the winners in the Idea track 2024. For this challenge, we integrate EO data, public news and ACLED conflict incidents to make prediction and extract feature importance that is highly related to conflicts in each state.

Our idea saw us integrate EO and open-source data to uncover conflict drivers using AI and NLP, delivering context-specific information to decision-makers through our state-of-the-art data extraction and integration pipeline.
